Deliberately did NOT file the September 8, 2026 Microsoft Patch Tuesday: apply-findings' dedupeKey() strips non-org/title words shorter than 4 chars and its isSameThing() gives events a 75-day drift tolerance, so a generically-titled monthly recurrence like 'Microsoft Patch Tuesday' on 2026-09-08 collides with the existing 2026-10-13 entry (35 days apart) and would silently overwrite October's date rather than add September as its own row. --dry-run confirmed this (it showed 'microsoft-patch-tuesday-2026-10' as updated, not a new entry added). This is the same dedup surface the 2026-08-28 run flagged for near-duplicates that don't merge; here it's the opposite failure mode, over-merging distinct monthly occurrences of anything titled generically enough. Whoever maintains apply-findings/id.ts should consider keying recurring monthly events (Patch Tuesday, earnings calls, etc.) by month instead of relying on the generic 75-day EVENT_DRIFT_DAYS tolerance.
